body: I have some additional information. 1. The import settings are unrelated. Simply the fact that the image got **reimported** reset the image, which fixed the issue temporarily. The import settings showing a `7` for the Roughness Mode is likely an unrelated bug. 2. The smearing is unrelated, and a result of how `blend_rect()` works when calling `image.blend_rect(image, recti, Vector2(0,1))`. Although `blend_rect()` should probably mention it does not blend the two images in one go, but instead loops and replaces each pixel one by one. However, why I reported this in the first place was because I commented out that line and tried exporting again, which lead to the same result, which meant the only conclusion was that `get_region()` was at fault. In fact, it seems to be that ``` @tool @export var cluster_texture : Texture func create_blend_image(): var image = cluster_texture.get_image() image.blend_rect(image, Rect2i(0,0, image.get_width(), image.get_height() / 2), Vector2(0,1)) ``` does not only adjust the `var image` but also the image as it was imported. You can see this when hovering the imported image and looking at the preview image. Which means, unless you reimport the image, the data set on the Texture is permanently changed. Note that the Inspector does still show the correct/original image: Now this should **NEVER** happen, because as the [`Texture2D.get_image()` documentation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_texture2d.html#class-texture2d-method-get-image) states, this returns a **Copy** of the data. It even explicitly states that a **new image is created every time**. So how can adjusting the image copy lead to the `@export` texture/imported texture being adjusted. Adjusting the script to `var image = cluster_texture.get_image().duplicate()` resolves the issue.

It seems only the `get_image()` call is affected, on both the `@export` reference to the texture and the `load(path)` reference to the texture. If you directly input the texture, the output visuals are unaffected. _Keep in mind this is **after** the image has been permanently adjusted by calling `blend_rect()` on the `get_image()` in the tool script_ I am unsure if this also happens with calls other than `blend_rect()`

This is the same underlying issue as https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/121173

The docs for `texture2D::get_image()` are wrong. It only sometimes returns a copy of the image. In many cases it returns a reference to the underlying image used by the texture. 

The docs should be updated. Off the top of my head, the behaviour is as follows (but whoever updates the docs needs to check manually):
1. NoiseTexture2D: always returns a reference
2. Other texture types return a copy when running the game but return a reference in the editor

The documentation should also be updated in the [`ImageTexture`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_imagetexture.html#description) class:
> Note: The image can be retrieved from an imported texture using the [Texture2D.get_image()](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_texture2d.html#class-texture2d-method-get-image) method, which returns a copy of the image:
